chapter: Chicago childhood: theaters, violin and first bass
title: The extended family and community that raised children
summary: Hinton and Taylor reflect on neighborly togetherness in Mississippi and Chicago and say it is missing today.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: For most people who lived there… it‟s difficult for anyone who didn‟t live through that to understand the difference between the extended family that you described, both in Chicago and in Mississippi, where you really did look out for your neighbor‟s children and your friends, and everybody was…
And this is still going on in Chicago. The ones that are my age are still…
Still have that attitude [unintelligible]. But that extended family, I find it‟s something we seem to be missing to this day.

I know my grandmother… if somebody was sick she would say, “Go take Ms. Jones this [unintelligible} and this soup over there”. And they would also tell on the kids if you were doing something wrong. Anybody could correct you and then they‟d tell your family about it.
